concerns: Risk that capture‑reagent/excipient incompatibility could confound attribution of loss to membrane damage—proposal correctly identifies and requires capture‑compatibility/spike‑in controls but these controls are preconditions and must be executed before interpretation (dependency).
Generalisability: proposal assumes MSC source‑cell lots represent production bank; evidence for cross‑lot reproducibility is not provided (dependency noted).

Translational limitation: macaque intranasal biodistribution negative result warns that preserving an analytic identity does not ensure in vivo detectability/bridging—proposal frames this as indirect support but additional large‑animal/administration validation will be required to link analytic gates to in vivo exposure.
Assay readiness: availability and orthogonal validation of an exogenous intact‑EV spike‑in (orthogonal species or label) is critical; lack of cited validation data is an execution risk.
conclusion: The proposal is internally consistent and appropriately attributes supporting literature as indirect support for the inference that downstream freeze-thaw × device-shear × excipient exposures can abolish an orthogonal intact‑EV analytical signature while leaving bulk particle counts similar. MISEV2023 is correctly cited for analytic rigor and assay-compatibility recommendations; the rodent MSC/EV studies (Hermann) are correctly characterized as program‑level preclinical examples of processing-sensitive efficacy; the macaque biodistribution study (Driedonks) is correctly used as limiting translational evidence cautioning that preserved analytic identity may still not yield detectable delivery in larger species. Inference statements are labeled in the proposal. No literature fact is misrepresented as SGL-001 experimental evidence.
evidence_gap: No direct experimental evidence is cited showing that the specific matrixed downstream exposures (defined freeze‑thaw cycles × device‑relevant shear profiles × named excipient classes) reproducibly abolish the orthogonal intact‑EV capture+particle co‑localization signature across ≥3 independent conditioned‑medium lots while spike‑in recovery confirms assay integrity. Additionally, there is no cited data demonstrating availability/validation of the proposed exogenous intact‑EV spike‑in tracer or capture‑compatibility panels for the specific excipient/device matrices and source‑cell material to be used.
